findings.claim: test_init_counts_unparseable_record and test_init_counts_records_in_subfolders did not assert init's exit code

verdict.text: The round 1 finding is fixed, and the rest of the change is the same as what passed review in round 1.
Both tests now assert `result.exit_code == 0, result.output` before they check the files.
The `ScaffoldResult` docstring is rewrapped and says the same thing.
Nothing else in the tree moved in a way that needs a new finding.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format, tests, integration and eval rows r1 to r4 all pass, "stamp green: b9ae168f864b2a6414f3517f6d8116b7464334d8cdf66d1dddfe9bf3c0fb50ed".
That matches the fingerprint the round's placeholder is bound to.
I re-read the whole uncommitted diff in the worktree (eight files).
`_write_first_decision` returns when `decisions.rglob("*.md")` turns up any file other than `index.md`.
If `decisions/` is missing, rglob yields nothing, so a fresh bundle still gets `0001`.
`_has_first_decision` and the `okf` import it used are both gone.
r3: `test_init_counts_unparseable_record` writes a record with broken front matter, checks exit code 0, and asserts the folder still holds only that record and `index.md`.
It would fail if init wrote a first decision next to it.

r5 (judgment): ADR 0011's "Correction, 2026-10-19", the `ScaffoldResult`, `scaffold()` and `_write_first_decision` docstrings, the init epilog and `docs/reference/commands.md` all state the empty-folder rule.
The docstring rewrap did not change that wording.
Both tests in `tests/test_init.py` now assert the exit code before they check the files, so a crash cannot pass for "nothing written".
